case_studies.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
case_studies.abstract: Understanding and reasoning over long contexts has become a key requirement for deploying large language models (LLMs) in realistic applications. Although recent LLMs support increasingly long context windows, they often fail to use relevant evidence that is already present in the input, revealing a gap between context access and effective context utilization. case_studies.title: Reasoning effort, not tool access, buys first-try reliability in agentic code generation: an observational study
case_studies.abstract: Agentic coding assistants are increasingly given extra capabilities, such as browser based testing tools and design oriented system prompts, on the assumption that more capability yields better software. This study tested that assumption directly. Ninety independent agent runs built the same application, a real time retrospective board, from one detailed specification, each scored on a fixed 14 criterion functional rubric (42 point maximum) and a visual quality review. case_studies.summary: This research study investigates whether giving agentic coding assistants more tools and capabilities directly results in better software reliability. The study found that the level of reasoning effort, not the access to tools, is a key factor in achieving first-try reliability in code generation. The researchers built and tested a real-time retrospective board application using different agent runs and model generations to reach this conclusion.

case_studies.abstract: Steering and monitoring activations in Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for both safety and interpretability. case_studies.title: The Rollout Infrastructure Tax in Coding-Agent Reinforcement Learning
case_studies.abstract: Coding-agent reinforcement learning treats execution infrastructure as a background implementation detail, despite relying on large numbers of interactive software rollouts. This is a missed opportunity: measuring infrastructure overhead can reveal practical efficiency gains for RL post-training, where small per-rollout savings compound at scale. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient infrastructure use in coding-agent reinforcement learning by measuring infrastructure overhead, the authors built a comparative study of four execution substrates, and the result shows significant variation in cold-start latency and costs. The study reveals practical efficiency gains for RL post-training. This affects cloud infrastructure management as it highlights the importance of optimizing execution infrastructure for reinforcement learning workloads.

case_studies.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Despite alignment training, LLMs remain prone to generating unsafe outputs at deployment time. Monitoring outputs online and raising an alarm when safety can no longer be assumed is therefore critical. We study a simple real-time monitor that turns a verifier signal from an external model into an alarm decision by thresholding, with the threshold calibrated via risk control. In experiments on mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets, we show that this simple design is competitive with more advanced monitors based on sequential hypothesis testing.
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of Large Language Models (LLMs) generating unsafe outputs by building a real-time monitoring system that raises an alarm when safety can no longer be assumed. The system uses a simple thresholding method to turn a verifier signal from an external model into an alarm decision. The result shows that this design is competitive with more advanced monitors.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM deployments, here is what to do: implement a real-time monitoring system to track output safety, set a threshold for alarm decisions based on risk control, and test the system using datasets like mathematical reasoning and red teaming.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper provides novel IT relevance by exploring real-time safety monitoring for LLMs, and its findings are potentially actionable for IT engineers working with LLMs. However, its value within 90 days is limited.

case_studies.title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
case_studies.abstract: We present WorldDirector, a highly controllable video world model framework designed for persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration. Unlike existing world models that entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering and rely on continuous visual observation to sustain motion, our framework explicitly decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of creating controllable world simulators by building a framework called WorldDirector, which allows for persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration, resulting in more realistic video world models. The researchers built a framework that decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation, allowing for more control over the simulation. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: When Do LLM Personas Support Visualization Design? A Cross-Model Study of Color Assignment and Chart Choice
case_studies.abstract: Large language model personas are increasingly used to approximate diverse users during early-stage visualization design, but it remains unclear whether persona-conditioned outputs reflect stable personality effects or artifacts of model choice and task framing. We examine this question across two visualization-relevant tasks: color assignment for abstract and concrete concepts, and chart-idiom preference ratings across task contexts. case_studies.summary: This research investigates how large language models can be used to simulate user personalities in visualization design, finding that model configuration greatly affects the results. It built a study to examine color assignment and chart choice across different models and tasks. The result shows that personality effects in visualization design are not stable across different models.

case_studies.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of overfitting in large language models by introducing a new method called Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation, which helps to reduce privileged information leakage. The authors built a new training method that allows the model to learn from its own disagreements, resulting in improved cross-domain generalization. This research is relevant to IT engineers managing cloud infrastructure that utilizes large language models.
